name: domainry-builder-v1
description: Build, evolve, repair, integrate, and verify a Domainry backend from accepted requirements or delivered frontend evidence. Use for metadata-first Domainry projects, frontend-to-Runtime replacement, Runtime integration, and full-stack defect routing. Keeps frontend evidence read-only except an explicitly authorized Data Exchange offline-export center.

# Domainry Builder V1

Each run owns one explicit Delivery Batch and follows exactly `requirements → model → apply → verify → done`. A batch is an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Keep one project-visible TODO at `.domainry/development/<session-id>.md`; copy [the template](assets/DEVELOPMENT_TODO.template.md) only when it is absent, then resume its `Current stage`. Do not invent stages, state files, or continuation workflows.

The accepted product scope remains the baseline: never silently reduce it to an MVP. Put stable Requirement IDs and Feature keys in the current batch, record deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership, and include every shared resource or regression boundary affected by the batch. `done` means this batch is complete, not that deferred product scope was delivered.

Resolve this file's directory as `SKILL_ROOT` and set `DOMAINRY_CLI="$SKILL_ROOT/bin/domainry-cli"`. Use only that packaged CLI. The workflow has exactly five commands: `model capability`, `model plan`, `apply model`, `apply finalize`, and `verify`.

## requirements

Read [requirements and domain truth](references/requirements-and-domain-truth.md) and the [PRD template](assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md). Settle domain truth inside this stage for the current batch and its dependency closure: actors and scope; objects, relations, states, defaults, and retention; commands, transactions, idempotency, calculations, and external effects; Reports and offline export intent; schedules, notifications, files, and integrations. Any required human approve/reject wait is a Runtime Workflow requirement, not two synchronous Handler branches. Any required downloadable Report export is a governed `report_export_controls` plus offline Data Exchange requirement, not a Report permission alone.

When frontend source exists, inspect it as evidence, including API Mock adapters, handlers, fixtures, seeds, and mutation side effects. `frontend/**` is read-only except for the authorized export-center slice described below. Treat it as evidence, not authority for missing policy. Record frontend defects for owner `frontend`; do not hide them with backend workarounds. Preserve the accepted product baseline in `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` and record a traceable current-batch delta with stable Requirement IDs, sources, owners, acceptance results, Feature ownership and deferred scope. Do not advance while an unresolved choice changes current-batch observable behavior, authorization, money/units, an irreversible effect, or state flow.

## model

Select the one task profile and comma-separated requirement topics from the accepted current-batch dependency closure, then request one exact minimum reading plan. Read every returned `read_order` path once, in order, relative to `SKILL_ROOT`; do not independently scan the [capability index](references/capabilities/README.md) or template tree. The returned documents, including [backend model](references/backend-model.md) when selected, remain authoritative—the plan replaces manual discovery, not their semantics. Preserve the complete current desired state in `backend/model/*.json` and referenced `backend/reports/*.sql`; prefer one Feature per model file, and change only current-batch Features plus the declared shared-resource closure. Never edit `domain/**` or `.domainry/**`, and never emit compiler-owned `capability_assembly`, standalone Permission definitions, versions, ownership, or seed metadata. Author each ordinary Role directly as an array of exact `<permission_key>;<data_scope>` grants.

Classify every writable Object as either plain `direct_crud`, or `action_only` plus a source-owned Handler for any named, conditional, derived, state-changing, side-effecting, or cross-record command. Do not author new Automation. A human approval must be an enabled Workflow graph with an approval task, authorized assignee resolver, explicit approved and rejected branches, and terminal Action effects; standalone approve/reject Handlers are not the waiting process. Reports use `object_sql_v1`; every required export also authors the Blueprint `report_export_controls` closure (bounded rows, audit/download Objects and mappings, requester-owned grants, assurance/masking when required) while Runtime Report and Data Exchange own execution.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --reading-profile <initial-delivery|feature-increment|handler-repair> \
  --topics <records,permissions,identity-profile,organization,reporting-line,workflow,scheduler,reports,report-export,notifications,connectors,agents,entrypoints,workspace-provisioning,files,domain-truth>
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model capability --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" [--key <category>]
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" model plan --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`model plan` performs one immutable load of the complete current model, validates the whole cross-resource draft, derives capability and authorization closure, persists deterministic diagnostics/provenance, and reports the Ledger change set. On failure, repair the complete stdout `diagnostics` batch using each file/JSON Pointer, constraint, actual/allowed value and hint before rerunning; its `artifact` path, relative to `--project`, retains the full provenance. Never guess a capability key: use the index's exact keys; Runtime execution-only modules have none. A Delivery Batch is not a loader or apply filter. Confirm that every create, update and delete belongs to the batch or its declared impact closure; repair the named owner and rerun. Once valid, keep the model unchanged while reviewing removals and evolution-sensitive changes.

## apply

Read [project mutation](references/project-mutation.md), then apply the reviewed model:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply model --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" \
  --go-module-path <domain-qualified-module>
```

Retain its immutable implementation packet. Read the compact packet index once: its `actions` array is the complete exact Action-context path list, `summary.shared_constraints` applies to every Action, and `summary.test_commands` is the copyable command contract for this delivery. Read its exact `verification.path` during apply—not after finalization—for the release-bound public Runtime route/auth/acceptance-fixture/evidence index and black-box example. Then read each compact Action context by exact path and follow that context's `read_order` once, in order, relative to `PROJECT_ROOT/backend`; those exact generated contracts and project-owned source/test files replace embedded source dumps and broad generated-tree scans. For this packet, implement only the project-owned backend source and paired tests, and create every required `backend/tests/businessflow` case for this batch. For a selected custom Connector, request its focused context with `model capability --connector-context <connector.provider>` immediately before implementation. Never edit generated source, manifests, receipts, caches, journals, or managed Runtime state.

The only frontend mutation exception is a Data Exchange offline-export center for an exportable Object SQL Report when `Frontend mutation scope: integration_authorized`; follow [its contract](references/frontend-offline-report-export.md). Otherwise report the owner gap.

Follow `summary.stage_boundary` literally: finish all project-owned source, then run `summary.test_commands.focused` and `summary.test_commands.business_flow_compile` before finalization; a full-tree failure caused by not-yet-generated composition is not an implementation failure. After both pre-finalize commands pass run `summary.test_commands.finalize`, then and only then run `summary.test_commands.full_tree`. These commands already contain the backend working directory, delivery build constraint, and project-local-plus-public hybrid `GOPROXY`; do not replace them with a default or local-only proxy. Once finalization succeeds, project-owned source is frozen for this verification attempt. Any later source change starts a new repair iteration and requires the focused/compile/finalize sequence again; do not continue the stale attempt into `verify`.

Finalize every delivered Handler and Connector:

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" apply finalize --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT"
```

`apply finalize` enforces source call-site contracts, including guarded `ConditionalUpdate`; do not add manual grep gates. Run the affected backend test set before advancing.

## verify

Read [evidence levels](references/evidence-levels.md), [verification](references/verification.md), and [Runtime integration](references/backend-runtime.md). The implementation packet's verification guide and every required business-flow test must already have been consumed/completed during apply. Verify is read-and-run only: do not create, edit, rename, or delete project-owned source after finalization. Every current-batch business flow and affected regression boundary needs a complete project-owned case with explicit preconditions, ordered actions, and a terminal durable result; denial cases also prove unchanged state. Unchanged flows may reuse only current baseline evidence. Run the highest-risk changed case against the managed Runtime before broader flow verification.

```sh
"$DOMAINRY_CLI" verify --json --project "$PROJECT_ROOT" --address 127.0.0.1:<port>
```

`verify` reuses structural/package receipts only after their complete source, model, Runtime and dependency identities validate; otherwise it runs the complete backend tree and rebuilds. It always proves healthy start and same-cohort restart, then leaves Runtime stopped and emits stage/cache telemetry. `backend/tests/businessflow` is a black-box Runtime package: it may use published Runtime HTTP/client operations but never import project Handlers, generated capability/data fakes, or database drivers. For both phases every BF01-BF08 test emits its structured evidence marker exactly as verification documents. Treat Runtime identifiers and principal/context values as opaque. A shared login, health, read, or Action-catalog probe does not prove another named flow; each claimed Runtime case must execute its own ordered Runtime journey and read back its terminal durable result. Approval cases start the Workflow, observe the task, prove unauthorized denial, decide both branches, and read back process/task/business state. Export cases query and prepare the governed Report export, follow the requester-owned Data Exchange job to completion/download, and prove another actor is denied. Verify only requirement-observable denial, scope, conflict, rollback, replay, restart, worker, Report, export, file, notification, and provider behavior. Do not create a project evidence ledger or generic acceptance runner.

## done

Set `Current stage: done` only when every current-batch finding is resolved and current receipts, tests, durable observations, and Runtime identity support the claim. Report batch identity and scope, delivery identity, changed files, tests, Runtime result, highest evidence level, deferred Requirement IDs, and explicit limitations without claiming deferred product work is complete.

Project-owned edits are limited to requirements/TODO evidence, declarative model/SQL, backend source/tests, and the authorized export-center exception. Recoverable failures stay in the current stage: repair the responsible owner and rerun the same direct command.
# Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

Each row is a confirmed PRD semantic execution contract, not a platform-generated case title. Runtime-owned identity/context values are resolved through their formal source and carried unchanged; every flow uses isolated setup so dependent cases cannot pass from residue. # Requirements and domain truth

Use only for the `requirements` TODO section. Produce the accepted backend dependency PRD and freeze domain facts before capability discovery. Do not load model, apply, verification, or acceptance authority at this stage.

## Backend dependency PRD

Preserve the full accepted product demand as the requirements baseline. For a new project, complete replacement, or existing project increment, create or update `docs/backend-requirements-prd.md` from `assets/BACKEND_REQUIREMENTS_PRD.template.md`, or record an equivalent traceable current-batch delta that references the unchanged accepted baseline. Never silently reduce product demand to an MVP.

One Delivery Batch may implement an initial Feature slice, Feature increment, cross-cutting evolution, or repair. Record its stable Requirement IDs, planned Feature keys, baseline delivery/model identity, allowed shared-resource changes and affected regression boundary. Requirements outside the batch remain explicit deferred Requirement IDs with planned Feature ownership; `done` closes only the batch. A Feature slice must be dependency-closed: include any shared Role, entrypoint, Object, Action, Report, lifecycle or authorization change required for its behavior to be valid and verifiable.

Settle domain truth completely for the current batch and dependency closure before capability discovery. Deferred slices need enough stable identity and ownership to remain visible, but their unresolved details do not block this batch unless they change its observable result, authorization, amount/unit semantics, irreversible effect, or state flow. A later batch reuses the accepted baseline and resolves its own delta instead of rewriting unrelated requirements.

A source is structured when its rules live in stable titled/numbered sections citable as `<doc> §N`. If one section states a rule completely, cite it rather than restating it. A reference-mode PRD still carries requirement IDs, classifications, owner/capability mapping, decisions, acceptance criteria, and the matrices, each row citing its source section.

Read frontend evidence, when present, in this order: route/page registry and user journeys; typed application API; Mock adapters/handlers and fixtures/seeds; state stores and hooks; form/list/detail/report components; permission/menu guards; tests and stories; visible copy. Also read the current explicit requirement and latest accepted product/design documents. Requirements inspection is read-only. Mock or visible behavior proves demand or a current assumption, not a business rule without higher-precedence evidence.

When the frontend is already implemented, do not stop at API method names or TypeScript types. Search for every API dependency's Mock implementation, including request handlers, success/error responses, fixture collections, seeded identities, mutation side effects, generated identifiers, relation keys, enum/status values, timestamps, totals, and nested objects. Reconcile those concrete values with component reads and writes. Add any evidenced missing object, field, relation, lifecycle state, query shape, or representative worked example to the PRD, with its exact source path and an appropriate classification. Preserve conflicts and optionality: Mock-only fields remain `recommended` or `open` unless higher-precedence evidence confirms them, and decorative/test-only values do not become domain facts.

Use this precedence while preserving every conflict:

1. explicit current user decision;
2. latest accepted requirement or design contract;
3. latest implemented frontend behavior;
4. typed API and Mock semantics;
5. frontend tests;
6. legacy/reference implementation.

Classify every item as `confirmed`, `recommended`, `open`, `frontend_only`, or `legacy_reference`. Extract actors, journeys, observable success, objects, fields, relations, queries, commands, states, permissions/scopes, errors/conflicts, calculations, transactions/idempotency, external effects, and presentation-only behavior. Every write operation names authorization, observable validation/error behavior, transaction boundary, idempotency/retry policy, durable result, and acceptance proof.

Build one traceability row per in-scope requirement: `demand evidence → requirement ID → Feature key → Runtime owner/capability → model resource or approved source gap → permission/data scope → acceptance journey`. Account for every backend-bound typed API operation and route touched by the batch; reference the accepted baseline for unchanged rows and preserve explicit dispositions for deferred rows. Matrix cells are phrases; do not repeat table facts in prose.

## Critical ambiguity

Classify every unresolved choice before capability selection. Only `business_blocker` blocks model authoring, and only for the smallest affected slice.

| Decision class | Boundary | Handling | Blocks model? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `business_blocker` | At least two concrete incompatible choices remain, and selecting one changes an explicitly required observable result, authorization allow/deny, amount/unit semantics, irreversible external effect, or business-state flow | Name the choices, affected requirements/model items, and obtain current user or accepted requirement authority | Yes, smallest slice only |
| `contract_discovery` | Runtime-owned formal code, canonical identity/context source, or accepted-fact-to-capability mapping | Defer discovery to the typed client/fixed capability contract; record a Foundation/Runtime gap if absent | No |
| `safe_implementation_decision` | Reversible technical choice preserving the accepted invariant | Defer to the published standard or record one conservative default and evolution path | No |
| `product_follow_up` | Product preference with a fallback that preserves required results | Record assumption, owner, fallback, excluded acceptance scope, and review trigger | No |

Security/privacy omissions default to least privilege, sensitive by default, and no export. An explicit broader-disclosure requirement remains a `business_blocker` until its authorization boundary is confirmed.

Use these nonblocking defaults without inventing product rules:

- Explicit exact decimals, comparisons, or sums do not require absent optional currency/unit/range metadata; block only a comparison/conversion slice where incompatible units change the required result.
- Explicit asynchronous approval may use an independent approval Object while the host remains unchanged until the terminal effect; missing edit/cancel/resubmit preferences are follow-ups.
- An explicitly immutable resource with no required business-role read needs no invented read actor; prove creation through a formal admin/seed path or persistence evidence.
- Weekday/morning intent with no timezone/holiday preference uses deterministic deployment timezone and standard weekday cron; block only explicit incompatible calendar outcomes.

## Domain truth design

Freeze domain facts before asking what Runtime can implement. When requirements contain calculations, historical facts, settlement, correction, or reversal, read [domain-truth-and-settlement.md](domain-truth-and-settlement.md) once and close its ownership, persistence, snapshot, trace, correction, and consumer decisions.

Financial, payroll, points, inventory-cost, and settlement facts remain reproducible after Settings change. If an event locks a result, define the write-side atomic action and immutable snapshot/ledger before its reports.

Before capability discovery, settle only the model-visible Report facts: the business question, Object SQL source of truth, parameters and defaults, result columns and meanings, authorization/audience, and whether export is required. Report query transport and export execution are Runtime-owned and stay out of the project model and PRD.

Every required Report export defaults to an offline Data Exchange job. When the project owns a frontend, the PRD also records the export-center route/audience and the actor-visible job-list/download outcome. If the active typed Runtime Client lacks the actor-owned Data Exchange export-job list, record a Data Exchange owner gap instead of inventing a route or browser-local list.

Verify the authorized Object SQL result, out-of-scope denial, offline job submission, actor-owned job-list visibility, and completed-file download when export is required. Do not turn Runtime execution internals into project acceptance cases.

Record any explicitly required current-database query-plan evidence and driver (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, `EXPLAIN FORMAT=JSON`, or `EXPLAIN (FORMAT JSON)`) as a business-flow verification obligation. Capability schemas are resolved during model routing; do not manufacture a separate platform gate catalog or case inventory.

# Domain truth and settlement

## Requirement boundary

Freeze business facts before capability discovery. Platform capabilities decide how accepted facts map to Runtime; they do not decide what the facts are.

| Kind | Meaning | Implementation consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Occurred fact | A completed business event and its event-time inputs, rules, and result | Persist when it occurs; correct by reversal or adjustment |
| Summary | A read-only aggregation of occurred facts | Use Object SQL; never own the formula that created the fact |
| Simulation | A hypothetical result under assumed inputs or rules | Isolate from official facts, ledgers, payroll, and reports |

For every material calculation, decide: Calculation Owner, Evaluation Time, Persisted Result, Policy/Rule Snapshot, Input Snapshot, Calculation Trace, Correction/Reversal Strategy, Downstream Consumers, and Report Source of Truth. Keep only the smallest affected modeling slice blocked when accepted evidence leaves at least two incompatible choices that change the explicitly required formula, amount/unit semantics, occurred-fact identity, correction behavior, or observable result. Exact decimal representation, a stated threshold, and summation remain modelable when optional currency, unit, or range metadata is absent; use nullable metadata and stated command preconditions, and do not invent conversion rules. Route Runtime-owned representations through contract discovery and reversible persistence, index, audit, idempotency, and concurrency mechanics through the `safe_implementation_decision` rule in [requirements-and-domain-truth.md](requirements-and-domain-truth.md#critical-ambiguity); those choices do not become product business ambiguity, but their later verification remains mandatory.

## Versioned settlement pattern

```text
Versioned Policy
  → Atomic Settlement Action
  → Calculation Snapshot
  → Immutable Ledger
  → Reversal / Adjustment
  → Object SQL Report
  → Offline Data Exchange Export
  → Payroll / Export Reconciliation
```

Use this pattern for an event that locks money, commission, points, inventory cost, or payroll input. In one transaction, the settlement Action must validate idempotency and authorization, resolve the event-time policy, and persist policy identity/version, the actual rule snapshot, input snapshot, ordered calculation trace, final result, immutable ledger entries, and audit/outbox effects. A later policy version affects only later events.

Never update or delete an original financial ledger entry to correct history. Append a linked reversal for cancellation/refund and a reasoned adjustment for an approved correction. Preserve `reversal_of` or equivalent lineage, the original ledger ID, actor, time, reason, and approval boundary. A locked payroll/export consumer records the ledger IDs or a governed scope/hash it consumed; later adjustments follow the explicit correction period instead of silently changing the locked result.

## Anti-patterns

- Repeating one formula across pages or several reports.
- Joining current Settings to recompute a historical financial result.
- Rendering absent or unproven facts as numeric zero.
- Giving summary, detail, page, payroll, and export different scopes or formulas.
- Allowing Settings changes to drift historical results.
- Omitting ledger-ID-level traceability across consumers.
- Building a project-specific report AST, metric DSL, or SQL generator.
- Authoring Runtime Report transport or export-execution internals in the project model.
- Using a second export-only query, a synchronous browser export, or treating Runtime mechanics as domain facts.
- Synthesizing an export-job list from browser memory or internal Data Exchange tables.

## Acceptance matrix

Cover applicable boundaries with event-time input, policy identity, snapshot/ledger IDs, trace, consumer result, and allow/deny evidence:

- policy version switch before/after effective time;
- business-day cutoff and cross-midnight events;
- multi-party allocation with deterministic remainder handling;
- full/partial refund and reversal lineage;
- correction after payroll or another consumer is locked;
- summary/detail/page/payroll/export reconciliation by ledger ID;
- cross-store and cross-entity permission/data-scope denial;
- Runtime restart and Settings change without historical drift.
- Object SQL result correctness, parameter semantics, and source-of-truth reconciliation;
- actor-owned offline export submission, export-center visibility, completed download, and cross-actor denial when export is required;
- truthful active, completed, failed, cancelled, expired, and denied frontend states supplied by the published Data Exchange projection.

# Backend model files

`backend/model/*.json` is the only model-authored backend metadata input. The
model writes business differences; Plane expands every structural default into
the complete Ledger, Blueprint, authorization, Runtime Manifest, version and
hash contracts. Never edit `domain/**`, rendered Blueprints, or `.domainry/**`
by hand.

Omit every compiler-deterministic value: schema defaults, constants, one-value
enums, keyed identities, fixed discriminators, empty optional contracts and
derivable references. These are compiler output, not model decisions. Author a
field only when requirements permit more than one meaningful value or the
business meaning cannot be derived uniquely; validation must not turn a
compiler-owned default back into required model input.

## V3 file contract

The only top-level fields are `project` and `modules`. Exactly one file declares
`project`; modules and features may be split across files, but a Feature key and
a resource identity may each be declared only once across the whole model.

Use this project-only fragment as `backend/model/00-project.json`:

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "item_submission",
    "name": "事项提交"
  }
}
```

A project-only fragment should omit `modules`; an empty `"modules": {}` is
accepted only on the same file as `project` for envelope compatibility. Do not
use that empty form in a feature-only file. A feature-only file omits `project`
and populates `modules.<module>.features.<feature>` with at least one Feature.

```json
{
  "project": {
    "id": "item_submission",
    "name": "事项提交"
  },
  "modules": {
    "core": {
      "features": {
        "item_lifecycle": {
          "requirement": {
            "statement": "操作员可以提交待处理事项。",
            "acceptance": [
              "提交成功后产生持久结果。",
              "失败时不得产生部分数据。"
            ]
          },
          "objects": {
            "item": {
              "fields": {
                "name": "text!",
                "status": "select![pending:待提交|submitted:已提交]=pending"
              }
            },
            "item_submission": {
              "fields": {
                "source_record_id": "relation!->item",
                "status": "select![recorded:已记录]"
              }
            }
          },
          "roles": {
            "item_operator": ["item.read;all", "item.submit;owner"]
          },
          "actions": {
            "item.submit": {
              "kind": "record_operation",
              "handler": {
                "reason": "必须原子更新事项并创建提交记录",
                "access": {
                  "item": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
                  "item_submission": ["create"]
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Delivery batches and file ownership

Whole-model validation does not require whole-product implementation. The files
currently present under `backend/model/*.json` are the complete desired-state
baseline for this delivery. A Delivery Batch is an authoring and verification
scope, not a loader or apply filter: preserve every previously applied model
file, then add or update only the batch's Feature files and declared
shared-resource closure. `model plan` and `apply model` continue to load and
validate the complete current model atomically.

Prefer `00-project.json` plus one Feature per descriptively named model file.
Several files may declare different Features under the same module. A Role,
entrypoint or other cross-cutting resource still has one owning Feature/file;
when it supports multiple Features, declare those stable keys through the
resource `requirements` override instead of repeating the resource.

The Feature key is also its Requirement identity. Moving one intact Feature to
another file does not change Ledger identity, but splitting or renaming a
Feature creates new Requirement identities, relinks affected resources and may
delete the old Requirement. Review that change with `model plan`; never treat it
as a mechanical file edit. For an already-applied oversized Feature, a valid
staged migration may retain the old Feature as a requirement-only umbrella,
move one resource group per batch to a new Feature, and temporarily link those
resources to both Requirement keys. Retire the umbrella only in a later,
explicitly reviewed destructive batch when it no longer represents accepted
product demand.

The V2 `items -> module -> kind -> item -> payload -> emits` envelope is not
accepted. Do not author `kind`, `status`, `depends_on`, `decisions`,
`requirement_keys`, `contract_version`, `capability_assembly`, or internal
Ledger item names. This project is not released yet, so there is no legacy
format fallback.

## Feature ownership and traceability

Every resource inside a Feature inherits that Feature's requirement. Plane
creates the requirement Ledger item, resource dependencies and behavior links.
Only a resource shared by multiple Features declares an override:

```json
{
  "item": {
    "requirements": ["item_lifecycle", "audit_requirement"],
    "fields": {"name": "text!"}
  }
}
```

`requirement` contains only `statement` and optional non-empty `acceptance`.
Behavior owner tuples and the no-executable reason are compiler output.

## Keyed identities everywhere

Every schema array whose item has a stable identity is authored as a keyed
object. The compiler sorts it, injects `key`, `id`, `object_key`, `path`, or
`connection_key` as required, and emits the strongly typed array. This includes
Objects, Fields, Roles, Actions, dictionary items, report parameters/result
columns, notification variables, Workflow inputs/nodes/edges, Automation
instructions and Agent resources. Repeating the identity inside a value or
using an identity-bearing array fails model loading.

Examples:

```json
{"input_fields": {"comment": "long_text!"}}
```

```json
{
  "graph": {
    "nodes": {
      "start": {"type": "trigger"},
      "finish": {"type": "action"}
    },
    "edges": {
      "start_finish": {"source": "start", "target": "finish"}
    }
  }
}
```

State transitions use their directed edge as identity, so duplicate edges are
structurally impossible:

```json
{"transitions": {"draft->submitted": "item.submit", "submitted->archived": {"workflow": "item.archive"}}}
```

Open maps remain maps. In particular Agent `input_schema`/`output_schema`
properties, Action/Workflow bindings, connector configuration and other
business dictionaries are not mistaken for resource arrays.

Author every platform-defined closed enum in its documented lowercase form.
Plane accepts mixed-case spellings for compatibility and canonicalizes them
before validation, including nested schema enums, Role scopes, Handler access
operations and field DSL vocabulary. This compatibility never applies to
identity-bearing keys or open business values; those retain their declared
case and stable identifiers remain strict lowercase.

## Field string DSL

Object Fields, Action `input`/`output`, Workflow inputs and Report SQL
parameters use the complete compact base grammar:

```text
<type>[!][->target][value[:label]|...][=default][;modifier[=value]]...
```

### Complete type and modifier quick reference

This is the single copyable reference for the field DSL. It contains every
supported field type and every Object-field modifier; capability references
should link here instead of repeating the table.

```json
{
  "active": "boolean=true",
  "amount": "currency!=0;precision=19;scale=2;currency=CNY;rounding=half_even",
  "effective_date": "date!",
  "starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00",
  "contact_email": "email!;max_length=254",
  "quantity": "integer!;min=1;max=999",
  "remark": "long_text;min_length=1;max_length=500;localized",
  "score": "number;min=0;max=100",
  "discount_rate": "percent;precision=5;scale=2;rounding=half_even",
  "contact_phone": "phone;pattern=^\\+[1-9][0-9]{7,14}$",
  "customer_id": "relation!->customer;cardinality=many_to_one;on_delete=restrict;inverse=invoices",
  "status": "select![draft:草稿|done:完成]=draft",
  "business_no": "text!;unique;indexed",
  "website": "url",
  "assignee": "user",
  "category": "select!;dictionary=case_category",
  "risk_level": "select!;value_domain=risk_level"
}
```

- `!` means required.
- A default belongs in the base specification before the first modifier:
  `currency!=0;precision=19`, never `currency!;precision=19;=0`.
- `relation` requires `->target` and never accepts a default.
- `select` requires a non-empty, unique stable vocabulary. Labels default from
  the stable value when omitted.
- Supported non-relation Object modifiers are `unique`, `indexed`, `localized`,
  `min_length`, `max_length`, `min`, `max`, `pattern`, `precision`, `scale`,
  `currency`, `rounding`, `cardinality`, `on_delete`, `inverse`, `dictionary`,
  and `value_domain`.
- A relation never accepts `unique`; use `cardinality=one_to_one`, which makes
  the compiler derive uniqueness.
- Unknown types/modifiers, duplicates, invalid values, out-of-vocabulary
  defaults and context-inapplicable modifiers fail closed.
- Field types, modifier names and closed platform enum values are
  case-insensitive on input and compile to their documented lowercase values.
  ISO currency codes compile to uppercase. Stable business identities such as
  field keys, relation targets, option values, dictionaries and value domains
  remain strict lowercase identifiers.

Common repairs are local to the rejected field string:

| Rejected | Use | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `"customer_id": "relation!"` | `"customer_id": "relation!->customer"` | A relation requires its target. |
| `"status": "select!"` | `"status": "select![draft\|done]"` | Select needs exactly one vocabulary source. |
| `"status": "select![draft];dictionary=status"` | Choose inline options or `dictionary`, not both. | Vocabulary sources are exclusive. |
| `"amount": "currency;precision=2;scale=3"` | `"amount": "currency;precision=19;scale=2"` | Scale cannot exceed precision. |
| `"amount": "currency!;precision=19;=0"` | `"amount": "currency!=0;precision=19"` | A default must precede every modifier. |
| `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03 09:00"` | `"starts_at": "datetime=2026-09-03T09:00:00+08:00"` | Datetime defaults use RFC3339. |

The CLI rejects an invalid string during model loading and reports the stable
diagnostic code, exact JSON path, field key and repair facts. Fix that string;
do not replace the compact field map with generated full field arrays.

Notification variables use only the restricted `<type>[!]` subset. Their types
are `boolean`, `date`, `datetime`, `email`, `number`, `text`, and `url`; they do
not accept select options, relation targets, defaults, or modifiers. A business
enum such as `select![approved|rejected]` is rendered text in a notification, so
author it as `text!` and retain the enum on its owning Object or Action field.

Plane expands Object fields to `key`, `name`, `type`, `required`, `config`,
`validation`, labeled `options`, `unique` and `default_value`. Human-readable
names default from stable keys (`item_submission` -> `Item Submission`). Object
descriptions also receive a deterministic non-empty default; provide explicit
text only when it carries real domain meaning.

Action fields use the same strings. Object-only modifiers are consistency
assertions whose source Plane uniquely infers from the owning Object and the
Handler access closure, as detailed below. This preserves the named
type/precision contract without exposing source pointers to the model.

## Actions and source-owned Handlers

An Action key is exactly `<object_key>.<action_key>`; Plane derives
`object_key`, the default name, audit metadata, same-key Permission and empty
contracts. The model decides `kind`, allowed business roles, business fields,
preconditions and whether a source-owned Handler is needed.

`object_create` is the Runtime-owned generic single-Object create and must not
carry a project Handler. Use `object_operation` plus Handler/access when an
object-scoped create must derive trusted owner/org values, coordinate multiple
Objects, or execute other project logic. All other supported Handler kinds and
their object/record invocation scope are listed in the Actions capability
reference. A Handler Action must not use the bare suffix `create`, `read`,
`update`, `delete`, `restore`, `import`, or `export`, because those exact
`<object>.<operation>` keys belong to Runtime Object Permissions. Use a business
verb such as `lead.register` or a qualified key such as `lead.create_owned`;
grant that exact Action key to the Role.

```json
{
  "invoice.approve": {
    "kind": "record_operation",
    "input": {"comment": "long_text!", "effective_date": "date!"},
    "output": {"status": "select![approved|rejected]"},
    "handler": {
      "reason": "Approval updates the invoice and durable decision atomically",
      "access": {
        "invoice": ["get_for_update", "conditional_update"],
        "approval_decision": ["create"]
      },
      "connector_calls": {"accounting_primary": "enqueue_invoice_sync"}
    }
  }
}
```

`handler.reason` is the only authored capability-gap/rationale statement.
Plane derives owner, trigger, scope, atomicity, rollback semantics, involved
Objects, read/write sets and transaction requirement. Do not author
`authorization`, `payload_fields`, `handler.data_access`, `handler.output`,
`audit_event`, empty defaults, or behavior tuples.

Keep a plain Action-only value as a plain field DSL such as `"reason": "long_text"`;
it does not need a backing Object field. When an Action field
uses Object-only modifiers (for example `max_length`) or Object-backed numeric
semantics, Plane infers its source from the owning Object plus the Objects in
`handler.access`, using the Action field's exact key only. The owning Object wins
over an equally named field elsewhere in the access closure; equally ranked
same-key fields fail as ambiguous. Plane never binds differently named fields
through Action verbs, prefixes, suffixes, stemming, edit distance, grammar, or
synonyms. When an Action input and persisted Object field represent the same
business datum, give them the same stable key, for example
`rejection_reason` end to end. Otherwise remove Object-only modifiers to keep
the Action value standalone. The diagnostic lists compatible rename candidates
without choosing one. Never author a source pointer or add a fake Object field.
This source is generated type/lineage reuse only; it does not copy an Object
field's runtime value into the Action payload.

Do not put protocol or infrastructure identifiers in Action input: `id`,
`request_id`, `trace_id`, `correlation_id`, `idempotency_key`, `workspace_id`,
`principal_id`, `record_id`, `route_id`, `tenant_id`, `session_id`,
`database_id`, `db_id`, and `row_id` are rejected. Record targets come from the
Action route, idempotency from `Idempotency-Key`, request identity from Runtime,
and new technical IDs from backend code. Stable business numbers remain
legitimate business fields.

## Roles, data scope and write ownership

Roles contain exact Permission grants, and every grant carries its own scope:

```json
{"reviewer": ["case.read;org", "case.approve;owner", "case_attachment.read;owner"]}
```

The only scope values are `all`, `owner`, `org`, `org_child`, and
`target_org`. The Role's same-key Action Permission is the only authored
allowlist. Plane reverse-derives `authorization.allowed_roles`, registers the
Action Permission definition, and never invents a Role grant or scope. Authoring
`Action.roles` is rejected as a duplicate source.

Object write policy is compiler-owned:

- an Object written by a Handler is `action_only` and has no Runtime CRUD
  behavior;
- every other Object is `direct_crud` and receives a Runtime CRUD behavior;
- a direct create/update/delete/restore Role permission or entrypoint mutation
  on a Handler-written Object is a blocking ownership conflict.

Plane expands Role grants into one scoped data-permission container per declared Role/Object.
That container is compiler-owned: the model declares each exact
Permission and scope once as `roles.<role>[] = "<permission_key>;<data_scope>"` and never repeats the
expanded Object policy.

Never author `config.write_policy`, role-level `data_scope`, `scope_overrides`,
`data_permissions` or `reference_permissions`. Handler roles use their explicit
same-key Action grant without receiving direct CRUD mutation permissions.

## Relation reference input

A `relation->target` field is also the complete model input for a reusable
reference selector. Plane derives an exact reference policy only when the role
can write the source Object and read the target Object; duplicate
source/field/target policies collapse to one stable identity.

The frontend calls
`GET /records/{sourceObjectKey}/fields/{relationFieldKey}/options`
with the raw user `query`. It never supplies a target Object, display field,
permission, SQL wildcard or `LIKE` expression. Runtime resolves the relation,
enforces the reference and target row/field policies, escapes `%`, `_` and the
escape character, then creates a parameterized case-insensitive contains
predicate. The component renders only the returned `{"id":"…","name":"…"}`
items.
